messages:
incident-bot: PROD ALERT: KV cache eviction rate spiked ~6x in us-west-2, continuous-batching queue depth increased. Page to oncall.
maya: taking this. seeing customer errors for a handful of tenants, spike started ~10:12 UTC. pinging infra metrics now.
jon: grabbing logs. looks like batch_window_ms jumped to 250ms for some shards, causing huge inflight batches -> cache blowouts on hot keys.
sasha: is this the adaptive-window feature we rolled last week? feature flag: feature.batch_adaptive_window_v2
maya: yes. initial hypothesis: adaptive window mis-estimated seq length distribution and expanded batch windows on heavy-seqlen tenants -> kv cache pressure and evictions.
liam: confirmed high eviction churn on shards serving AcmeCorp and OmniPay. eviction TTLs dropping from 30m -> 2m.
maya: customer impact: elevated p50/p95 latency (p50 +45ms, p95 +220ms), 502 spikes for some streaming calls. severity: P1 degraded for those tenants.
sasha: can we do a quick per-customer override? We have per_cust_batch_configs that can pin batch_window_ms per tenant.
maya: plan: 1) enable immediate per-tenant override for affected customers (set static batch window 20ms) 2) toggle feature.batch_adaptive_window_v2 off for us-west-2 3) roll a hotfix to batch config defaults and canary it 5% -> 25% -> 100% 4) notify affected customers.
jon: I can push the per-cust override now for AcmeCorp and OmniPay.
jon: run:
```
rctl batch-config set --tenant AcmeCorp --batch_window_ms 20 --reason "mitigation: adaptive window causing cache blowup"
rctl batch-config set --tenant OmniPay --batch_window_ms 20 --reason "mitigation"
```
deploy-bot: Received request to set per-tenant batch config for AcmeCorp and OmniPay. Applying.
deploy-bot: ✅ batch config updated for AcmeCorp and OmniPay (propagated to edge pools in ~15s).
maya: good. observing drop in eviction rate for those tenants, latency improving. still seeing cluster-wide noise.
sasha: I'll flip the adaptive flag off in us-west-2 only. Command:
```
flagctl set feature.batch_adaptive_window_v2 false --region us-west-2 --note "rollback hotpatch"
```
deploy-bot: flag update queued -> applying...
deploy-bot: ✅ feature.batch_adaptive_window_v2 = false (us-west-2). Rolling change to routing nodes.
maya: metrics: eviction rate down 60% from peak after per-tenant + flag off. p95 latency trending down but not back to baseline yet.
kevin: do we need to limit batch growth too? maybe cap max_batch_size to avoid microbatch amplification.
jon: agree. pushing a quick hotfix to defaults: set max_batch_size 64 -> 32 and batch_window_ms default 100 -> 50. Canary to 5% first.
sasha: config snippet for hotfix:
```
{
  "batch_defaults": {
    "batch_window_ms": 50,
    "max_batch_size": 32,
    "kv_eviction_threshold": 0.75
  }
}
```
maya: execute canary. Monitor token/sec, eviction rate, 5xx rate, and queue depth. If any metric regresses >20% in 10m, rollback.
jon: triggering canary via deploy tool:
```
deploy-bot deploy batch-config --canary 5 --config-file hotfix-310111.json --reason "mitigate cache blowout"
```
deploy-bot: Canary started (5% of routing). Will report status every 2m.
deploy-bot: Canary health: OK (2m)
jon: initial canary looks fine. no immediate regression. promoting to 25%.
deploy-bot: Promoting canary to 25%...
deploy-bot: Canary health: degraded on one replica in us-west-2a: queue depth spike. Investigating.
maya: pause promotion. revert that replica to last stable.
jon: rolling back the affected shard. command:
```
deploy-bot rollback --replica us-west-2a-03 --to stable
```
deploy-bot: Rollback executed. Replica stabilized.
maya: since one AZ had a transient spike, we'll continue canary in the other AZs at 25%, but hold full rollout. ops, please keep an eye.
support-ops: opening support incident for AcmeCorp and OmniPay; sending templated note: "investigating increased latency and intermittent errors, mitigation in progress; will update in 30m." :white_check_mark:
support-ops: status page draft ready: "We observed elevated cache evictions affecting request latency in us-west-2; mitigation underway."
kevin: do we need to add a per-customer rate cap as a last-resort? If eviction pressure flares again, we can throttle microbatch arrival for specific tenants.
maya: good idea. keep as fallback. I'll set a temporary token_rate_limit for heavy tenants if needed.
liam: monitoring: p95 returned to +30ms above baseline for most tenants, but AcmeCorp now near baseline. eviction metrics stable.
jon: if we can get two consecutive 10m windows with no re-regression, we can promote to 100%.
sasha: agree. I'll prepare the rollout plan in case we need to revert quickly: have patch + rollback IDs and per-cust override ready.
maya: timeline: per-cust overrides applied at 10:14 UTC, flag off at 10:18, canary started 10:22, paused 10:28, rollback of bad replica 10:30, resumed 10:34 at 25% in healthy AZs.
maya: next actions: 1) keep canary at 25% for 20m 2) support to notify customers every 30m 3) SRE to collect heap/eviction logs for postmortem 4) designate postmortem owners.
kevin: i'll own the postmortem write-up with liam.
support-ops: will send next customer update in 25m. assigned on-call support: sasha.
deploy-bot: Canary metrics at 10:50 UTC: OK. No eviction spike, 5xx within threshold.
maya: promoting to 100% in 5m if no regression.
deploy-bot: Promoting to 100% now...
deploy-bot: ✅ Rollout complete to us-west-2. All canaries healthy.
maya: full rollout complete. cluster eviction rate stabilized near baseline. p95 latency back to normal range for most tenants.
jon: saved snapshots/logs for the affected timeframe: s3://redwood-ops/incident-31011122/logs.tar.gz
sasha: created temporary dashboard showing per-tenant eviction + batch window history.
support-ops: AcmeCorp notified and updated status page. no escalations from customer.
maya: summary: root cause likely an edge-case in adaptive window heuristic that caused over-expansion of batch_window_ms under skewed seqlen distribution for a few tenants, amplifying KV cache pressure -> evictions -> latency. mitigations: per-tenant override, flag rollback, hotfix to defaults, per-tenant rate cap as fallback.
kevin: postmortem owners: kevin, liam. timeline: start drafting, include reproducer, mitigations, long-term fix (tweak adaptive heuristic + safety caps), and runbook updates.
maya: closing incident thread here. will keep monitoring. thanks all. :rocket:
